                    ### Question
                    A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents for a routine colonoscopy. A polyp is found in the patient's transverse colon and is found to be cancerous on histological evaluation. Upon examination, it is found that these cancerous cells have decreased MHC class I expression on their surface. Which immune system cell is most capable of killing these tumor cells?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Natural killer cells
opb. B-cells
opc. Macrophages
opd. Eosinophils
ope. Cytotoxic T-cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the context of decreased MHC class I expression on tumor cells, the immune system cell most capable of killing these cells is the natural killer (NK) cell. Standard medical consensus indicates that cytotoxic T-cells require MHC class I molecules to recognize and kill target cells. When MHC class I expression is reduced, cytotoxic T-cells are less effective. However, NK cells are specifically activated by the absence or low expression of MHC class I molecules, as they recognize this as a sign of abnormality. The retrieved evidence paths support this by showing interactions between NK cells and tumor cells with altered MHC class I expression. Therefore, NK cells are the most capable of targeting and killing these tumor cells due to their ability to detect and respond to the lack of MHC class I, aligning with the corrected reasoning chains.
